claims.claim: Independent BUB1B reagents support target attribution
claims.support: Ten distinct reagent IDs have distinct annotated 6-mer and 7-mer seeds.
claims.challenge: Alternative processing, potency and unintended targets remain unmeasured; distinct annotations alone do not establish independent biological effects.
claims.falsifier: Alternative mature products or target-engagement measurements reveal shared effects or lack of intended knockdown.
claims.stop: Do not qualify the perturbation based on IDs or annotations alone.
claims.reopen: Sequence-aware and independently measured target/function evidence.
claims.next_action: Include sequence/seed records, independent perturbation and restoration controls.

claims.claim: The public BUB1B expression signature is predominantly on-target
claims.support: HT29 retains positive conditional coherence and target-transcript reduction.
claims.challenge: 45/54 evaluable BUB1B reagent-context records have stronger different-target/same-seed than same-target similarity, separately in both spaces.
claims.falsifier: Matched off-target controls reproduce the claimed downstream functional effect without relevant BUB1B deficit.
claims.stop: No drug rescue inference from expression coherence alone.
claims.reopen: Joint deficit/drug testing in an independently qualified model with functional recovery and injury endpoints.

claims.claim: The earlier failed reproducibility filter excludes useful BUB1B signal
claims.support: The fixed v19 full filter still fails in all 14 contexts.
claims.challenge: HT29 retains a processed six-reagent excess-coherence signal in the v23 batch reference; v19 also retained a five-provider-reagent partial positive.
claims.falsifier: Independent target-specific functional validation succeeds despite the earlier filter failure.
claims.stop: Do not equate operational filter failure with biological disproof.
claims.next_action: Keep HT29 as a limited orthogonal-qualification lead, without transfer to non-cancer tissue or the child.

claims.claim: A zero reference tail establishes strong confirmation
claims.support: Four positive-coherence seed-reference results exceed every enumerated control set.
claims.challenge: Finite seed references often contain only 4–40 sets; add-one sensitivity removes all five primary threshold crossings across the fixed 36-test family.
claims.falsifier: Coverage, null matching or multiplicity sensitivity removes the apparent support.
claims.stop: No calibrated FDR/probability claim; no promotion from zero exceedances.
claims.reopen: Prespecified adequately covered controls plus independent confirmation.
claims.next_action: Retain original and sensitivity results together; prespecify handling of finite references and missing controls.

claims.claim: Orthogonal reference agreement validates the BUB1B/everolimus proposal
claims.support: The PRIME analysis places intended genes first in 21/297 comparisons and MTOR within ranks 1–13 of thousands of RNAi references.
claims.challenge: No BUB1B CRISPR observation, no joint drug/deficit experiment, selected targets, engineered-parent differences and dependent observations.
claims.falsifier: BUB1B perturbation/restoration or joint drug/deficit functional testing fails in the intended model.
claims.stop: No cross-gene transfer of biological qualification or drug benefit.
claims.reopen: Direct BUB1B and drug/function evidence satisfying v21 safeguards.
claims.next_action: Use MTOR as a method/mechanism reference while validating BUB1B and non-cancer function separately.
